front: What was the Great Leap Forward?
back: The 1958-62 campaign to raise farm and industrial output rapidly by mass labour, communes and backyard furnaces; it led to famine.
Student groups mobilised by Mao from 1966 to attack officials, teachers and old culture in the Cultural Revolution.

front: How many people died in the Great Leap famine?
back: Estimates range from about 15 million to 45 million or more (poor records); the true number is unknown.
9 September 1976; the Gang of Four was arrested in October.

front: What was the Hundred Flowers campaign?
back: In 1956-57 Mao invited criticism of the Party; when it went too far, the Anti-Rightist Campaign punished critics in 1957.

front: When did China explode its first atomic bomb?
back: 1964, after the Soviet Union withdrew its advisers and refused nuclear help.

front: Why did the Great Leap Forward fail?
back: Unrealistic aims, mass labour instead of skill, false reports by frightened officials and bad weather.

front: Why did Mao launch the Cultural Revolution?
back: To regain authority after the Leap, to remove 'capitalist roaders' and to renew revolutionary spirit.

front: What links the Sino-Soviet split to southern Africa?
back: ZANU and ZANLA looked to China, ZAPU and ZIPRA to the Soviet Union.
